questions.stem: Highlight the findings that support pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

perOption.r5: Excludes ectopic pregnancy; does not support PID.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

perOption.r1:c2: Needs IV antibiotics and possibly drainage.

exhibits.body: Admit to gynecology. Interventional radiology to review the abscess.

questions.stem: Which actions should the nurse take about the client's partners and reporting? Select all that apply.

options.text: Report gonorrhea and chlamydia to the health department
Encourage the client to tell recent partners so they can be treated
Offer expedited partner therapy where state law allows
Call the partners and tell them the client's name and diagnosis
Tell the client that partners only need treatment if they have symptoms

rationale.correct: Report, notify and treat partners while protecting confidentiality.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.educationalObjective: Take action on STI reporting and partner treatment.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll finish 14 days of doxycycline even when I feel better."
"I'll avoid sex until my partners and I finish treatment."
"I'll take doxycycline with a full glass of water and stay upright."
"I'll take doxycycline with milk to protect my stomach."
"Birth control pills protect me from STIs."

rationale.correct: Full course, abstinence until partners treated, correct doxycycline use and condoms.
references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The treatment is {{b1}}, and if the client had a penicillin allergy and were pregnant, the plan would be {{b2}}.

options.text: one dose of benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM
penicillin G procaine with bicillin C-R mixture

rationale.correct: Benzathine penicillin; in pregnancy, desensitize and give penicillin.

perOption.b1:a: Treats primary, secondary and early latent syphilis.
perOption.b2:a: No alternative is adequate in pregnancy.

questions.stem: How should the nurse give benzathine penicillin G? Select all that apply.

options.text: Deep IM into the ventrogluteal site
Observe the client for 30 minutes afterward
Give it IV to make it act faster
Give it into the deltoid to reduce pain

rationale.correct: Deep IM into a large muscle, never IV, with observation.

perOption.a: Large muscle for a thick suspension.
perOption.d: IV benzathine penicillin can cause cardiac arrest.
perOption.e: The volume is too large for the deltoid.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

exhibits.title: Order
exhibits.body: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM once.

questions.stem: Six hours after the injection, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Explain that this expected reaction settles within a day
Recommend acetaminophen for fever and aches
Ask the client to call back if it lasts over a day
Record a new penicillin allergy in the chart
Repeat the penicillin dose because the rash got worse

rationale.correct: Fever and aches within hours of treatment are a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction.

rationale.correct: Falling titer shows response; reinfection and neurologic symptoms need attention.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate its cause in falciparum malaria.

columns.text: Infected red cells sticking in small vessels
Parasite use of glucose and quinine-type drugs

rationale.correct: Sequestration and hemolysis explain the organ damage.

perOption.r4:c1: Sequestration and hemoglobin in the tubules.
perOption.r4:c2: Sequestration and hemoglobin in the tubules.
perOption.r4:c3: Sequestration and hemoglobin in the tubules.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse's first action is {{b1}}. The antiparasitic drug of choice is {{b2}}.

options.text: treat the hypoglycemia with IV dextrose

rationale.correct: Correct the glucose, then start IV artesunate.

perOption.b1:a: Low glucose worsens the confusion and can kill.
perOption.b1:b: Not needed for the first drug.
perOption.b1:c: Resistant and the client cannot swallow safely.
perOption.b1:d: Malaria is not spread person to person by air.
perOption.b2:b: For liver stages of other species, after G6PD testing.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

perOption.e: Can cause pulmonary edema in severe malaria.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: To theater now. Vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, clindamycin IV.

questions.stem: During the first vancomycin infusion, the client develops flushing and an itchy red rash on the face and neck. Blood pressure is unchanged. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Restart later at a slower rate, over at least 60 to 120 minutes, if ordered
Record vancomycin as a lifelong anaphylaxis allergy
Speed up the infusion to finish before the rash spreads

rationale.correct: Flushing with a fast vancomycin infusion is an infusion reaction; slow it down.

perOption.e: This is an infusion reaction, not anaphylaxis.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
